about: Invented nights for tests and examples only (R2). None is anyone's. Every night a test or a plan uses lives here.

waking.text: I started a new job at the library this week. My sister moved to Lisbon in October!
sentences: I started a new job at the library this week.
My sister moved to Lisbon in October!

waking.text: We painted the kitchen green last weekend... It still smells of paint.
sentences: We painted the kitchen green last weekend...

dreams: A lighthouse stood in the middle of a wheat field, and its lamp turned slowly even though it was noon. I walked toward it but the field kept getting wider.
Then I was in a kitchen with green tiles, sorting buttons into jars by colour. One jar would not close.

waking.text:
I have been walking to work since the bus route changed
The mornings are colder now.
sentences: I have been walking to work since the bus route changed

dreams: I had a dream that a paper boat carried me down a staircase of water inside an old library.

waking.text: Vi flyttade till en ny lägenhet i september. Jag har börjat sjunga i en kör!
sentences: Vi flyttade till en ny lägenhet i september.
Jag har börjat sjunga i en kör!

dreams: Jag stod på en perrong där tågen var gjorda av glas, och varje vagn var full av små citronträd.

waking.text: Har jag berättat att vi fick en hund? Hon heter Selma.
sentences: Har jag berättat att vi fick en hund?

nights.name: Glastrappan
dreams: En trappa av glas gick upp genom molnen.
Sedan cyklade jag över en frusen sjö med en kopp te i handen.
Till sist hittade jag en nyckel i fickan som passade i alla dörrar.

waking.text: The exam is on Friday. Dr. Lind said it would be short. “It is only an hour.” she told us. Prices went up 2.5 percent?! ... I keep forgetting my keys
sentences: Lind said it would be short.

dreams: A copper bell hung from the branch of an orange tree, and every time the wind moved it the oranges changed colour, first to blue, then to grey, then back again. I climbed the tree to stop the bell, but the branches kept growing longer under my hands, so the bell was always one arm away. Below me a crowd of tortoises carried lanterns across a frozen river, and none of them looked up.
